# Ledgerstone: an embedded relational database with SQL in Rust

> Ledgerstone is an embedded relational database in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, small enough to read end to end.

Ledgerstone has real tables with typed INTEGER, TEXT, and REAL columns, rows persisted to a single file on disk, and a hand-written SQL parser and executor, all in one readable crate with no server process and no C library underneath. It supports CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT with WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT, UPDATE, and DELETE, with typed errors for bad SQL, wrong value types, or missing tables and columns, and it never panics on malformed input. A database is one file, so copying the file copies the whole database.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone wants a readable, from-scratch reference for how storage, SQL parsing, and execution fit together in a single Rust crate.
- An AI agent wants a local SQL store it can query over stdio; the mcp mode runs an MCP server exposing a ledgerstone_query tool.
- It is a teaching-oriented database, the version of SQLite you can open in an editor and follow, not a production engine.

## Interfaces
- CLI and REPL (ledgerstone --db), an HTTP API (serve --port, POST /query returns JSON), and a Model Context Protocol server (mcp mode, ledgerstone_query tool).
